**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back, showing moderate to severe ear rot
- Kernels appear brownish-tan with pinkish/reddish discoloration across most of the ear
- Husks appear bleached/dried
- The rotted area appears to affect the entire ear with a pinkish-reddish tinge to the kernel coloration

**Reasoning through candidates:**
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to pink-red mold, typically starting at the tip via silk channel — matches the pink/reddish kernel coloration
- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting from the BASE of the ear + bleached husks + black pycnidia — bleached husks match but the pink coloration doesn't
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon scattered mold with starburst pattern — possible but coloration here is more broadly reddish than scattered

The pinkish-reddish kernel discoloration throughout the ear, combined with the bleached husks and the ear-wide mold pattern, is most consistent with **Ear_rots_Gibberella**. The reference collage shows highly decomposed Gibberella-affected ears with similar overall brownish-pink rot patterns. The pink/reddish kernel streaking is the key distinguishing feature from Diplodia (white mold) and Fusarium (scattered salmon spots).
